description.p: Skribisto helps you write anything, from a novel to course notes, without fighting formatting along the way. Organise a project in a binder tree of folders and items; the book's structure — Part, Chapter, Scene, Note — comes from the role you give each row, not from where it sits in the tree. Every writing row keeps its prose and its synopsis side by side.
Skribisto is not a word processor: a project exports to DOCX, ODT, EPUB, PDF, HTML, Markdown, Djot, LaTeX or plain text, so the final formatting happens in whichever program you prefer.

ul.li: Dual editor pane (prose and synopsis), with split panes and tabs
Read a whole chapter, part or book as one continuous document, or every synopsis at once
Corkboard, writing sessions, pace tracking and manuscript analysis
Search and replace across the project, trash with restore and undo, autosave and backups
Spell checking with downloadable dictionaries, light and dark themes, per-editor typography
Open several projects at once, each in its own window

ul.li: The folder Skribisto keeps its backups in is created when the app starts, so the location shown in Settings is really there before the first backup is taken
Show folder, in Settings under Backup defaults, opens that folder itself instead of the one above it
French typography no longer confuses the spell checker: the thin space inside « » and before ?, ! and ; is not taken to be part of the word next to it
New binder, in the outline's binder menu, asks for a name before it creates anything, so Cancel no longer leaves an unwanted binder behind
Your text replacement rules are loaded when a project opens, so they fire from the first keystroke instead of staying dormant until you added a new one
Search options and history are restored with the project you open, instead of reverting to the application defaults and overwriting what the project had saved

Format ▸ Formatting mark places the invisible characters typography needs: a no-break space, a narrow no-break space, a no-break hyphen, a soft hyphen, a zero-width space and a word joiner, four of them with a keyboard shortcut
